We expect to incur significant expenses related to commercial operations, manufacturing, supply chain, medical affairs, distribution and potential future launches outside the U.S.

We expect to continue to incur apitegromab development costs as we invest in trials to support other SMA patient populations, such as our Phase 2 OPAL clinical trial, and for programs in multiple other diseases beyond SMA where selective inhibition of myostatin activation may offer therapeutic benefit, such as our Phase 2 FORGE trial.
We expect to incur costs to support our anti-myostatin program, and our Phase 1 trial for SRK-439.
Additionally, we will support the development of our pipeline and any other nonclinical programs.
Furthermore, we expect to continue to incur costs associated with operating as a public company.

Based on our current operating model, we expect that our existing cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, together with the cash available under our debt facility and our anticipated product revenues will enable us to fund our operating expenses and capital expenditure requirements into 2028.
However, we will require additional capital in order to complete clinical development and commercialization for each of our current programs.
We have based this estimate on assumptions that may prove to be wrong, and we may use our available capital resources sooner than we currently expect.
Accordingly, we will need to continue to rely on additional financing to achieve our business objectives.

Until such time, if ever, as we can generate substantial product revenues, we expect to finance our cash needs through a combination of equity offerings, debt financings, collaborations, strategic alliances and licensing arrangements.
